races.title: State Assembly, District 24
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Alex Lee
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly since 2020, representing District 24 (Fremont, Newark, Milpitas, Sunol and parts of San Jose). Former legislative policy advisor to State Sen. Henry Stern. Chairs the Legislative Progressive Caucus. UC Davis graduate and former student body president.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, Equality California, California Environmental Voters, YIMBY Action and Our Revolution.

cands.gaps: We found no votes, bills or statements from Lee on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land buying, gun laws, police pay and pensions, school vouchers or teacher pay. We found no documented position on slowing growth or protecting open land beyond his general pro-housing statements. His campaign site and Ballotpedia profile give no specific date for his development-related statements. The sources describe no controversies from his time in office. A Wikipedia entry about a 2015 student-government dispute is not backed by a news source we could read, so we left it out.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born in San Jose and split his childhood between Milpitas and North San Jose, and he describes himself as born and raised in the district.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since December 2020 and chair of the Legislative Progressive Caucus. Earlier he was a full-time legislative policy advisor to State Sen. Henry Stern (2017-2019) and held internships with several legislators.
qual.why: Nearly six years of legislative service plus a prior career as a legislative policy advisor on state policy, which is a high fit for writing law and the budget. His Budget Committee seat and committee chair role are not counted.
qual.label: Nearly six years of legislative service plus a prior career as a legislative policy advisor on state policy, which is a high fit for writing law and the budget. His Budget Committee seat and committee chair role are not counted.

clean-money.evidence: Introduced AB 20 on his first day in office, a bill to ban corporate donations to political candidates.

workers-first.evidence: Co-authored AB 1675 (2026), the No Tax Breaks for ICE Contractors Act, which would end tax breaks for California companies contracting with ICE.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site lists protecting reproductive freedom as a priority and says he was named a NARAL Reproductive Freedom Champion.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 3 priorities; 2 backed by their record, 0 only promised

roots.summary: Wikipedia says he was born in San Jose and split his childhood between Milpitas and North San Jose, and he describes himself as born and raised in the district.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: His campaign site says he promotes smart growth policies creating more mixed-use housing in dense areas, and supports social housing (AB 11 of 2025). Wikipedia describes him as a strong supporter of legislation to increase housing.

cands.name: Max Hsia
cands.bio: Max Hsia is the 2026 Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 24. Public pages give no occupation or prior offices. His campaign site describes a focus on 'common sense policies' and community events.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Republican Party of California and Reform California, plus several voter guides and media recommendations (April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn).

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Max Hsia was born or raised, or when he came to California. We couldn't find his occupation, work history or any elected office he has held. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and his campaign site says little about specific policies. We found no stated positions or documented actions on data centers, development, property taxes, housing ownership, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. We found no reported controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: No job, business or elected-office history appears in the pages reviewed.
qual.why: His work background could not be established from the available pages, so he is not scored.
qual.label: Background not found: unknown, not unqualified
